title: implement-federated-signal-normalizer-and-granular-cutover-policy
author: Rina Kapoor
description:
Motivation: Recent rollouts showed transient baseline shifts across regions and tenant cohorts that caused noisy canary signals and premature rollbacks. This PR adds a federated signal normalizer to reduce cohort-level baseline variance and a granular cutover policy to enforce phased traffic migration with rollback budget accounting.

What this changes: Implements a normalization stage that consumes per-cohort latency and throughput fingerprints, fits a lightweight robust linear transform (median-based) per-slice, and exposes a normalized delta used by the canary evaluator. Adds a new CutoverPolicy primitive that accepts traffic tiers, staged percentages, cooldown windows, and a rollback-credit budget. The canary orchestrator now uses normalized metrics to compute regression scores and consults the CutoverPolicy before advancing traffic.

Design notes: The federated normalizer operates at two time resolutions: fast (1m) and slow (1h) rolling windows. Each cohort contributes a sketch (p50/p90/p99, qps) to the aggregator; the transform is computed using a robust estimator to avoid being dominated by bursts. The normalized delta is the difference between candidate and baseline after applying cohort transforms and a global shrinkage factor to control sensitivity. CutoverPolicy enforces minimum-successful-probe-counts per stage, consumes rollback-credit on failed stages, and supports emergency-abort hooks.

Backward compatibility: New behavior is gated behind a config flag perf.canary.federated_normalizer=false by default in existing deployments. The CutoverPolicy is available to rollout plans but does not replace existing simple cutover configs.

Testing: Unit tests for transform math and edge cases (empty cohorts, zero traffic) included. Integration harness added that replays historical traffic traces (prod replay + synthetic drift) to validate reduced false-positive rate. End-to-end canary sim shows a 42% reduction in noisy rollbacks on our historical dataset.

Migration & rollout: Feature flagged. Plan: enable in canary lab for two weeks on non-critical namespaces, then enable for low-traffic customers, monitor stability dashboards and rollback budget consumption metrics.

Checklist:
- [x] Algorithm implementation
- [x] Unit tests
- [x] Integration replay tests
- [x] Config gating and docs
- [x] Observability (new metrics + dashboards)

Related: ENG-4210 (reduce noisy canary rollbacks), SUP-9123 (customer incident analysis), ENG-4302 (cutover policy RFC)

review_conversation: Sanjay Rao: Can you clarify how the shrinkage factor is computed? Looks like a tunable hyperparameter - suggest adding a sensible default and a brief comment about tradeoffs.
Rina Kapoor: Added comment and default (0.6). The shrinkage is AggShrink = max(0.1, min(1.0, median_scale * 0.6)). Updated docs section with rationale.
Marta Liu: Integration tests are failing intermittently in CI; seems related to replay trace ordering. Can we ensure deterministic seed in synthetic generator?
Rina Kapoor: Fixed seed and added additional assertions to the replay harness. Re-ran CI - green.
Ethan Brooks: Approving after verifying metrics emission and dashboards. One nit: move the metric name prefix to 'perf_canary.'
Rina Kapoor: Applied rename and force-pushed. Thanks!
release_notes:
- Add federated signal normalizer to reduce cohort baseline noise for canary evaluations.
- Introduce CutoverPolicy for staged traffic migrations and rollback-credit accounting.
- Feature gated behind perf.canary.federated_normalizer flag (disabled by default).
